Title: Sacrorum conciliorum nova, et amplissima collectio, in qua praeter ea quae Phil. Labbeus et Gabr. Cossartius S.J. et novissime Nicolaus Coleti in lucem edidere, ea omnia insuper suis in locis optime disposita exhibentur, quae Joannes Dominicus Mansi evulgavit. Tomus Secundus: ab anno CCCV ad annum CCCXLVI
Creator: Giovanni Domenico Mansi (ed.), after Philippe Labbe, Gabriel Cossart and Nicolas Coleti
Publisher: Facsimile reproduction for H. Welter, Paris and Leipzig, of the Florence edition 'expensis Antonii Zatta Veneti'
Publication Date: 1901 (the facsimile: 'Editio iterata ad Editionis principis exemplum ab Huberto Welter ... M.D.CCCCI' at file line 233; the original edition of this volume is catalogued by archive.org as 1759)
Rights: Public Domain (pd-us-by-date: the 1901 facsimile date is printed at file line 233; the underlying edition is of the 18th century); the item record carries no rights field
Language: lat (Latin, with the Greek of the conciliar texts printed in the original; the OCR renders the long s as f)
Source: archive.org item sacrorumconcilio0002phil (catalogue title 'Sacrorum Conciliorum Nova, Et Amplissima Collectio.', volume 2, catalogue date 1759, language tag eng), full text at https://archive.org/download/sacrorumconcilio0002phil/sacrorumconcilio0002phil_djvu.txt. Fetched directly 2026-10-17 by the Shared-Events source-research thread; the byte count of the downloaded file (5,066,834) equals the size archive.org lists for the djvu.txt.
Provenance note: Extracted unaltered: the item's own djvu.txt is reproduced whole after this header; nothing was stripped, normalized or corrected, so scan notices and OCR errors remain as scanned. Rights basis: the 1901 facsimile date read in the OCR of the title page places the printing out of US copyright under this project's pd-us-by-date rule; the text reproduced is that of the 1759 edition, older still. Same printing and same vendoring discipline as the tomus 3 and tomus 4 files already in this directory.
Content note: The second volume of Mansi's conciliar collection, councils of 305 to 346: by its own headings 'CONCILIUM ARELATENSE' (Arles 314, file line 430, with the canons and the synodal letter to Silvester) and 'CONCILIUM NICAENUM GENERALE' (file line 599; the creed, canons, synodal letter, Constantine's letters, the subscription lists and the Latin versions of the canons, with the editors' dissertations), then Ancyra, Neocaesarea, Gangra, Antioch, Tyre (335), Jerusalem, Rome under Julius and Antioch (341). The whole-collection Latin and Greek witness for Arles and Nicaea; the Greek column's OCR recovery was not checked line by line.
